facts.claim: In document authoring, a block is a table whose first (header) row carries the block name; the content model is the row/cell structure authors fill in beneath it.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks ('authored as a table with a heading as the first row that identifies the type of block'); https://www.aem.live/docs/authoring ('a table with a merged first row that serves as the block name'); delivered as nested <div> rows/cells
facts.question: In document-based authoring for AEM Edge Delivery Services, how does an author create a block and tell the system which block it is?

facts.claim: Block variants are authored in parentheses after the block name in the header row (e.g. 'Hero (Dark)') and become extra CSS classes on the block element; comma-separated options become separate classes, multi-word options are hyphenated.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks#block-options ('Columns (dark, wide)' -> class="columns dark wide", 'Columns (super wide)' -> 'columns super-wide'); live aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c search.plain.html 'Search (minimal)' -> class="search minimal"; da-content references/html-content.md:211-223 agrees
facts.question: How does an author mark a style variant on an EDS block in a document, and what does it become in the rendered markup (including multi-word and multiple variants)?

facts.claim: Visual/behavioral differences of a block should be expressed as block variants rather than as configuration rows/cells (use 'Hero (Dark)', not a 'style | dark' row).

facts.question: For an EDS block that needs, say, a light and a dark appearance, what authoring mechanism does the platform provide for the author to pick the appearance?

facts.claim: Name/value (key/value) rows in a block should be reserved for true configuration (behavior/data-fetching settings), not for content; modeling displayed content such as heading, image or text as labeled name/value pairs (e.g. 'text | ...', 'author | ...', 'image | hero.jpg') is an anti-pattern.
facts.source: SKILL.md:72, SKILL.md:117, SKILL.md:122, references/canonical-models.md:11, references/canonical-models.md:186, references/canonical-models.md:203-211, references/canonical-models.md:235-251, references/canonical-models.md:439, references/canonical-models.md:446-459, references/canonical-models.md:495

Rule #14 does not restrict configuration to API-driven content, as the skill's 'API-driven content ONLY' wording does
facts.question: What does aem.live's content-modeling guidance (David's Model) say about using name/value pairs inside blocks?

facts.claim: A configuration-style block is laid out as two columns per row: the key in the left cell and the value in the right cell.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L233-263 readBlockConfig (cols[0] -> toClassName key, cols[1] -> value; links -> href, images -> src, multiple -> array); ue-component-model SKILL.md:54-56 ('key-value': true for 2-column key/value blocks)
facts.question: How is a configuration-style (settings) EDS block laid out in the authored table, and how does the boilerplate read it?

facts.claim: AEM Edge Delivery has 4 canonical block models: Standalone, Collection, Configuration and Auto-Blocked.
facts.verified: partial: no aem.live page names this taxonomy (checked www.aem.live/query-index.json, 268 pages; davidsmodel, markup-sections-blocks, block-collection, component-model-definitions, examples/how-to-use-auto-blocking). The underlying patterns are documented separately: list items as rows of a block table (davidsmodel Rule #5), name/value config (Rule #14), auto blocking (markup-sections-blocks#auto-blocking)
facts.quiz: excluded: taxonomy is the skill's own framing, not a documented platform fact

facts.claim: Hero is a standalone block: a hero image plus an H1 heading (with optional text/CTA); image and text may sit in one cell or separate rows/columns.
facts.verified: live https://main--aem-block-collection--adobe.aem.live/block-collection/hero.plain.html (one row, one cell: <picture> + <h1>); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 blocks/hero/hero.js is empty (CSS-only), so layout comes from authored semantics

facts.claim: A blockquote is a standalone block: the quote text in one row and the attribution in a following row (italic), with styling via variants rather than 'style'/'background' rows.
facts.verified: partial: the Block Collection block is named Quote, not Blockquote; live aem-block-collection quote.plain.html 'Quote (with attribution)': row 1 quote text, row 2 attribution ('Attribution, Source' - only the source is italic, not the whole line); plain Quote has a single row

facts.claim: Auto-blocking turns default content authored outside any table into a block programmatically, based on pattern detection, so authors never see block syntax.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks#auto-blocking ('Auto blocking turns default content and metadata into blocks without the author having to physically create them ... programmatically creates the DOM structure of a block')
facts.question: What is 'auto blocking' in AEM Edge Delivery Services?

facts.claim: Auto-blocking logic is implemented in the project's scripts.js.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks ('The code for your projects auto blocking lives in buildAutoBlocks() in your scripts.js'); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/scripts.js:L80-104 buildAutoBlocks, called from decorateMain before decorateSections/decorateBlocks
facts.question: Where in an EDS project does auto-blocking code live, and when does it run relative to block decoration?

facts.claim: A YouTube link pasted as plain content can be auto-blocked into an embed block.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks#auto-blocking ('an author linking to a YouTube video by simply including a link ... embed block'); https://www.aem.live/examples/how-to-use-auto-blocking (buildEmbedBlocks). Note: not shipped by default - aem-boilerplate@5cea543 and aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c scripts.js only auto-block fragments and widgets; BC Embed is an explicit block
facts.question: How can an author get a YouTube video embedded on an EDS page without authoring a block table, and what makes that work?

facts.claim: When auto-blocking a YouTube embed, an image immediately preceding the URL becomes the preview/poster image; the result is <div class="embed embed-youtube"> with picture and link cells; without an image the block still works.
facts.verified: partial: aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c blocks/embed/embed.js uses a inside the block as a click-to-play placeholder, otherwise lazy-loads via IntersectionObserver (so 'works without an image' holds); but the 'embed-youtube' class is set by embed.js at load time (block.classList = `block embed embed-youtube`), not by auto-blocking, and aem.live's auto-blocking example (examples/how-to-use-auto-blocking) wraps only the bare link - grabbing a preceding image is custom project code. Delivered images also carry elements, unlike the shown
facts.question: In the Block Collection's Embed block, what happens if the author places an image in the block next to the video URL, and what happens if there is no image?

facts.claim: Auto-blocking suits frequent, predictable, reliably detectable patterns; rare, varying or hard-to-detect patterns should be explicit blocks.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/examples/how-to-use-auto-blocking ('When to use Auto-Blocking': appear frequently, authors naturally write as plain content; 'When to use Explicit Blocks': pattern varies, authors need control, requires options, rare enough that auto-detection would be brittle)
facts.question: According to aem.live, when should a content pattern be auto-blocked rather than authored as an explicit block?

facts.claim: Authors create section breaks with '---' (a horizontal rule) in the document.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/authoring ('--- (three hyphens) on a single line'; Google Docs Insert -> Horizontal Line); https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks ('separated by horizontal rules or ---')
facts.question: How does an author create a section break in a Word or Google Docs page for EDS?

facts.claim: A Section Metadata block placed in a section carries name/value pairs; its 'style' value (e.g. 'tabs') becomes CSS class(es) on the containing section, which code can detect.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/block-collection/section-metadata (name/value pairs -> data-* attributes; Style -> class attribute; Id -> id); live https://main--aem-block-collection--adobe.aem.live/block-collection/section-metadata.plain.html renders <div class="light"> (applied by the HTML pipeline; no section-metadata code in aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js); https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks#sections
facts.question: What does a Section Metadata block do to its section, and how is its 'Style' property treated compared with other properties?

facts.claim: Consecutive sections whose section metadata has 'style | tabs' are merged by auto-blocking into one tabs block: each section becomes a tab, its H2 the tab title and the rest the tab content.
facts.verified: partial: https://www.aem.live/developer/component-model-definitions describes the pattern (complex components like tabs/accordions 'modelled as sections and combined together using auto-blocking client side'; a 'tab' section type combining consecutive sections with a tab-title data attribute), but it is project code: neither aem-boilerplate@5cea543 nor aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c scripts.js implements it, and the Block Collection Tabs block is an explicit block (one row per tab: label cell + content cell, tabs.plain.html, blocks/tabs/tabs.js)
facts.question: How is the Block Collection's Tabs block authored, and what alternative pattern does aem.live describe for tabs whose panels must contain other blocks?

facts.claim: Blocks inside sections that are auto-blocked into a container (e.g. tabs) are preserved as nested blocks, so tab content can mix default content and blocks.
facts.verified: partial: possible only with custom container code - aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L590-591 decorateBlocks only decorates 'div.section > div > div', so a block div moved inside another block (by buildAutoBlocks, which runs before decorateBlocks) is neither decorated nor loaded unless the container code handles it
facts.question: Which elements does the boilerplate's block decoration treat as blocks, and what happens to a block element that ends up nested inside another block?

facts.claim: EDS does not support nested blocks (no table inside a block table); content allows only one level: a section contains default content and blocks.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks ('Blocks should never be nested'); https://www.aem.live/developer/component-model-definitions ('deliberately allows only a single level of nesting'); https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #2; da-content references/html-content.md:81, :339
facts.question: Can an author put a block inside a cell of another block in EDS? What nesting does the content model allow?

facts.claim: Container components that need to hold other blocks (tabs, accordions) are modeled as separate sections that auto-blocking combines into one block.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/component-model-definitions ('in order to have more complex visual components that can contain other components, they have to be modelled as sections and combined together using auto-blocking client side. Typical examples of this are tabs and collapsible sections like accordions')
facts.question: Given EDS's nesting limit, how does aem.live recommend building container components such as tabs or accordions whose panels contain other blocks?

facts.claim: Fragments - linking from a block to a separate document that holds the inner blocks - are an alternative to nesting blocks.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #2 ('Consider fragments (referencing other documents) or links (with auto blocking) to reduce the authoring complexity'); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/scripts.js:L82-98 auto-loads links containing /fragments/ via blocks/fragment/fragment.js loadFragment (fetches <path>.plain.html)
facts.question: Besides auto-blocking, what does aem.live suggest instead of nesting one block inside another, and how does the boilerplate pull such content in?

facts.claim: Fragments fit nested content that is complex, reused across pages, or managed separately.
facts.verified: partial: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #12 'Fragments may be harmful': good for content used across many pages (header/footer, sign-up form, legal disclaimer), but they add indirection for authors (worse when nested) and SEO-relevant content should be on the page itself; 'complex nested content' alone is not given as a reason
facts.question: What does aem.live's content-modeling guidance say about when fragments are appropriate and what they cost authors?

facts.claim: Fragment references inside block cells can be written as relative links (e.g. '../fragments/getting-started').
facts.verified: partial: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #4 'Fully qualified URLs only' (authors paste full URLs; code extracts the pathname); the pipeline rewrites same-site links to root-relative (BC fragment.plain.html href="/block-collection/fragment-include"); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 blocks/fragment/fragment.js only loads paths starting with '/' (uses getAttribute('href')), so a '../' href would be rejected by the fragment block
facts.question: What form of URL does aem.live recommend authors use when referencing other content (fragments, pages, data) from a document?

facts.claim: Don't require authors to build formal lists for list-like content with complex items; model each item as a row of a block table (collection) because complex list items are hard to author in Word/Google Docs.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #5 ('list items that are more complex, are somewhere between hard to practically impossible for an author to keep in a list ... much easier to have the list items be rows of a block table ... cards block in the boilerplate')
facts.question: According to aem.live's content-modeling guidance, how should a block that holds a list of complex items (e.g., related articles each with image, title and link) be modeled, and why?

facts.claim: For simple list items, never require a formal list: support one item per paragraph in a single cell or one item per row, and let decoration code accept both.
facts.verified: partial: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #5 says that for simple lists (text, possibly with a link, or plain links) a list in Word/Google Docs 'may be ideal', or a single cell containing all the links (code just pulls all links); it does not say to avoid lists for simple items
facts.question: For simple items (plain text or links) inside a block, what authoring forms does David's Model consider acceptable?

facts.claim: Decoration code can render rows authored as a collection into semantic <ul>/<ol> output.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 blocks/cards/cards.js (builds a <ul>, one <li> per authored row)
facts.question: How does the boilerplate Cards block turn its authored rows into semantic HTML?

facts.claim: Spreadsheets in AEM are published as JSON that block code can fetch.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/spreadsheets (ingested via preview and served as JSON at the corresponding .json path; single-sheet vs shared- multi-sheet formats); live https://main--aem-block-collection--adobe.aem.live/block-collection/form.json
facts.question: What does AEM Edge Delivery do with a spreadsheet an author previews or publishes, and how can site code use it?

facts.claim: Spreadsheet-based forms: a Form block holds a link to a spreadsheet (published as JSON) that defines the fields; the block fetches it and builds the form; the Block Collection has examples.
facts.verified: partial: aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c Form block: row 1 link to <form>.json (columns field, type, label, help, options, placeholder, default, conditional, required), row 2 submit URL; form.js fetches it. But https://www.aem.live/developer/block-collection lists Form as 'Block (Deprecated)' and aem.live now steers forms to widgets (https://www.aem.live/docs/widgets) or Edge Delivery Services for AEM Forms (https://www.aem.live/developer/forms, license required)
facts.question: How is the Block Collection's Form block authored, and what is its current status in the collection?

facts.claim: Blog listings and search results are typical Configuration-model blocks driven by key/value settings.
facts.verified: partial: https://www.aem.live/developer/block-collection and markup-sections-blocks now say self-contained application-like functionality (a form, search results, a calculator) is a widget referenced by a single link to /widgets/<name>/<name>.html (query params -> data-* attributes), not a block (aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/scripts.js buildWidgetAutoBlocks); the Block Collection Search block is one cell with a link to query-index.json, not key/value rows. Key/value config blocks remain valid (readBlockConfig)
facts.question: How does aem.live currently recommend implementing application-like features such as search results or forms on an EDS site?

facts.claim: A good content model works across authoring surfaces; structures that only work in one authoring tool are an anti-pattern.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Introduction ('A good way of testing a content model is to imagine an author working in different environments (eg. Word, Google Docs, AEM, Custom Authoring etc.) and making sure that the content model can easily be constructed ... across all possible content sources')
facts.question: According to aem.live's David's Model, how should one test whether a content model is good?

facts.claim: Too many columns in a block row is an anti-pattern: it hits horizontal space limits and usually means content was split into small values instead of using default-content semantics (headings, paragraphs, links).
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #10 'Limit number of Columns' ('practical horizontal screen / document size limitations ... usually a symptom that content is split into small values that do not reflect a proper use of default content and the implied HTML semantics'); Rule #3 limit row/column spans
facts.question: What does aem.live's content-modeling guidance say about the number of columns in a block table, and what does a high column count usually indicate?

facts.claim: Infer variants and values from the content and use smart defaults instead of requiring authors to enter data that could be inferred.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #1 ('Often variants or blocks can be inferred, meaning that for example a carousel containing a video or a quote with an image should not be its own (explicit) block or variant but can be inferred automatically from the content')
facts.question: What does aem.live's David's Model say about making, for example, 'carousel with a video' its own block or variant?

facts.claim: Developers, not authors, should absorb structural complexity: decoration code should tolerate variations in how authors arrange content instead of forcing rigid structures for developer convenience.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks#blocks ('developers absorb the complexity of translating an intuitive authoring experience into the DOM ... It is often tempting to delegate complexity to the author ... An author should always be able to simply copy/paste a block and intuitively understand what it is about')
facts.question: In aem.live's guidance, who should carry the complexity of turning authored content into the DOM a block needs, and what should an author always be able to do with a block?

facts.claim: If a block's functionality matches a Block Collection block, reuse/look up that block's content model.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #11 ('Use the block collection content models ... the content model should be similar'); https://www.aem.live/developer/block-collection ('The primary value of these blocks is the content structure they provide')
